claims.interpretation_notes: Final position: Supported, unchanged from round 1. PRIMARY (agenda placement; Council or committee; one count per service package; cost stated): P=3, C=3, U=0. (A) Integrated service package 'Improved Accessibility - Active Pathway Snow Removal and Sidewalk Repair'. FCS03158 Attachment 2, DocumentId 278877 (re-listed as 280346), pp. 27, 43-44. City Council agenda 2025-11-24, item 7.2 (an addendum item, added at adoption in minutes item 1.4; exact publication day not fixed, latest possible date 2025-11-24). First dealt with by Council 2025-11-25 (presentations and questions under items 7.1-7.3 together). Proposes raising SNIC priority in socially vulnerable areas, plus enforcement and sidewalk repair. Stated cost: 'a $2.11 million one-time capital investment, an annual ongoing operating increase of $1.60 million to prioritize SNIC efforts ... $1.64 million to enforcement services, as well as $4.59 million for proactive Sidewalk Maintenance repairs'; table: 2026 New Budget $9,938K, 35.2 FTEs. Establishes an excess over an identified approved budget: no. (B) Standalone service package 'Parking Ban Enforcement Strategies and Resource Allocation'. Same attachment, pp. 25, 34; same agenda and the same first-dealt date. Proposes contracted towing during parking bans; $100K ongoing in 2026. Its text says it 'improves service levels for snow and ice control'. Excess over an approved budget: no. Counting B is a judgement on a borderline case: it continues towing first funded one-time from 2025 Council contingency, and its lead branch is Community Standards. (C) 'Well Maintained City' service package. CO03513 Attachment 9, DocumentId 304812, and report 304803. CPSC 2026-08-31, item 7.1. First on a published agenda by 2026-08-22 per the archive capture the brief identifies (I have not verified it independently); first dealt with by the committee 2026-08-31. Proposes an eight-day residential blading window, a Priority 1 Cycle Crew, an event snow team, and enforcement. Stated cost: 'approximately $23.6 million in ongoing operating investment and $11.5 million in one-time capital funding', which also covers non-snow work (turf, sweeping, graffiti, inspections). Excess over an approved budget: no. The rung is robust to losing either B or C, but not both. Not counted: the C409L policy recommendation (the report says it needs 'no additional budget'); the 2026-27 operational changes the report says are within the current budget; the Winter/Summer positions package (no stated snow service change); and the $2.1M fleet inflation adjustment in FCS03158 (maintains service, does not change it). Counting the first two would raise P but not C or U. Attachment 10's 24 optional enhancements are not a separately presented service package, so they belong under the alternative unit. The commenter was probably thinking of CO03513 (the package plus its enhancements). Under the primary unit that is one proposal, so the verdict reaches two partly through the Fall 2025 packages. The verdict is about the proposition as defined, not the commenter's referent. ALTERNATIVES (one rule changed at a time): considered by a body by 2026-08-27: A and B considered by Council 2025-11-25; P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported (Partially supported if B is excluded, which is luna's result). Window to 2026-10-02: P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported under both timing rules (the 2026-08-31 motions requesting future packages are motions, not proposals). Pre-election start 2025-01-01: CO03079 (CPSC 2025-08-11 item 7.3) is counted once with A as an earlier version of Option 3, and CS02945 once with B; P=3, C=3, U=0, Supported, bounded to the record carried. City Council alone: A and B on Council's 2025-11-24 agenda; Well Maintained City reached Council only on 2026-09-08; P=2, C=2, U=0, Supported (Partially supported without B). Separately costed options: 24 (Attachment 10) + 3 packages = P=27, C=27, U=0, Supported; 24 are counted by the attachment's title, and on my reading items 19, 20 and 22 (catch basins, sweeping flushers) are not snow service changes. Stricter cost reading: no counted text in the window states an approved snow and ice budget and the increase against it; P=3, C=0, U=0, Contradicted. In this case that rung means only 'no baseline stated in the text'. It does not mean no new money was asked, because each package is expressly incremental or unfunded. The only stated baseline, CO03079's '$67 million/year' (2025), sits outside the primary window. Exactly two: C=3, Partially supported. The finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE: the stricter cost reading and the exactly-two rule each change the rung, and the story must say so beside the verdict. Under my count the two timing rules give the same rung. Even so, any reader-facing 'already put' should name the agenda-placement rule, because the third package had only been placed on an agenda, not considered, by 2026-08-27. Framing note (not material): the ladder's Contradicted wording ('what had been put states no new spending') misdescribes the strict-reading result here, and the story should not use that wording. The brief assigns no verdict on the four parked claims. For context only, CO03513 costs 'Calcium Chloride System Upgrades' at $2.5M ongoing and $4.4M one-time, and none of the four 2026-08-31 committee motions names calcium chloride.

limitations: In this round I worked from the carried texts and did not re-fetch the eScribe filestream or meeting pages. Other reviewers report that those pages return a browser check or HTTP 403 to automated tools, so the agreement among reviewers on what the files say is not independent retrieval.

Only 4 of the 36 sections of FCS03158 Attachment 2 were carried, chosen by the keywords snow / active pathway / parking ban / SNIC. I have not read the other 32 sections, FCS03158 Attachment 1, or private Attachment 4. A snow service package whose text uses none of those keywords is unlikely, but I cannot exclude one. Any such package could only add to C, and Supported is already the highest rung.

I read the first Not established condition ('a report or an attachment that could hold a proposal ... cannot be read') as applying where an unread file could move the rung. Under the primary readings it cannot: C is already at least 2 and the ladder has no rung above Supported. The files that hold counted proposals were carried whole or by complete section. On a strictly literal reading, unread files such as CS03123 (CPSC 2026-01-19) or CO03513 Attachments 1-8 and 11-13 would block the verdict. I flag this reading for the editor.

claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported, under the published-agenda rule. In November 2025 Council had before it two unfunded packages that Administration prepared at councillors' request: an active-pathway snow and sidewalk package with about $1.6M a year for snow clearing within a roughly $9.9M first-year total, and $100K a year for parking-ban towing. The result depends on definitions: if the proposal must state the approved budget it exceeds, no document qualifies, and if the count must be exactly two, the answer is partial because there are three.
